key_insight: Wan-Dancer proposes a hierarchical music-to-dance generation framework that can produce minute-scale, rhythm-coherent dance videos instead of stopping at short clips. The core idea is to manage long-range motion with a multi-level structure, reducing drift and keeping identity and beat alignment consistent over time.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the difficulty of generating long-duration, high-definition dance videos directly from music, especially when existing diffusion-based methods break down beyond ~20 seconds and suffer from temporal drift, identity inconsistency, and repetitive motion.
method: Uses a hierarchical framework to split long dance generation into manageable levels of temporal control.
Aligns motion generation with music rhythm to maintain coherent choreography over minute-scale sequences.
Aims to preserve subject identity and avoid repetitive or unstable motion patterns during extended video synthesis.
impact: This matters for practitioners because it pushes music-to-video generation from short demo clips toward realistic long-form content creation. It provides a direction for building more stable, temporally coherent generative systems for entertainment, virtual performers, and avatar animation.

paper_title: Wan-Dancer: A Hierarchical Framework for Minute-scale Coherent Music-to-Dance Generation
paper_authors: Mingyang Huang, Peng Zhang, Li Hu, Guangyuan Wang, Bang Zhang
